Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Houston/Galveston TX
516 AM CDT Tue Aug 4 2026

...New AVIATION...

.KEY MESSAGES...

- Seasonably hot with highs in the 90s and heat index values
  101-108F each day.
  
- An isolated late day shower can't be ruled out along the
  seabreeze, but most locations will remain dry.
  
- Slightly better rain chances expected Thursday into the weekend
  with some deeper moisture moving in from the Gulf. 

&&

.DISCUSSION...
Issued at 1153 PM CDT Mon Aug 3 2026

Clear to partly cloudy skies and warm temperatures anticipated 
tonight with lows in mainly in the mid to upper 70s inland and the
upper 70s to lower 80s along the coast. There is a chance for 
some isolated patchy fog early Tuesday morning, but chances are 
low. Fog, if any, will burn off quickly shortly after sunrise. 

Weather conditions will remain hot and on the dry side through 
mid-week as the mid to upper level ridge remains situated over 
Arizona, New Mexico, and extends into Texas. Expect the highs to 
peak in the upper 90s inland (some isolated spots reaching 100 deg
F) and the lower to mid 90s along the coast through Wednesday. 
Heat indices will peak between 103-108 deg F...thus, make sure to 
continue to protect yourself, your loved ones, and pets from the 
heat. From Thursday into the upcoming weekend, the highs are 
expected to range in the lower to mid 90s inland (although some 
spots could peak in the upper 90s) and the upper 80s to lower 90s 
along the coast. 

Subsidence will help limit rain chances early in the week. 
Slightly better chances for showers (20-40%) are expected mid week
into the upcoming weekend as surface moisture moves in from the 
Gulf waters and increases PWs. A good portion of these showers 
are expected to develop near/along the seabreeze during the 
afternoon to early evening hours. 

Cotto 

&&

.AVIATION...
(12Z TAF Issuance)
Issued at 516 AM CDT Tue Aug 4 2026

Satellite and observations reveal low-end MVFR ceilings currently
over CLL and approaching UTS early this morning. Can't entirely
rule out these reduced ceilings extending into CXO by sunrise.
Additionally, periods of patchy fog have brought reduced
visibility to LBX as well. VFR conditions will return area-wide by
15Z. Light SSW winds this morning will become S to SSE in the
afternoon with wind speeds approaching 8-12 kt. Isolated SH/TS
possible this afternoon between 21Z-01Z mainly around the Houston
metro terminals. Winds trend back towards light and variable
overnight with potential for another round of patchy fog and
reduced ceilings mainly west of I-45 going into Wednesday morning.
Ceilings/visibilities improve back to VFR by 15Z on Wednesday with
S to SE winds around 8-12 kt prevailing. Another round of isolated
afternoon SH/TS will be possible.

Batiste

&&

.MARINE...
Issued at 1153 PM CDT Mon Aug 3 2026

Light to occasionally moderate onshore winds and seas of 1-3 feet
are expected through the upcoming weekend. A slight increase in
rain chances can be expected during the weekend. 

Cotto

Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Lake Charles LA
1157 PM CDT Mon Aug 3 2026

...New DISCUSSION, AVIATION, MARINE, FIRE WEATHER...

.KEY MESSAGES...

- Dewpoints will begin to rise through the work week, while both
  high and low temperatures are forecast to remain at or slightly
  above average.

- Isolated diurnally driven afternoon thunderstorms will be possible
  each day through the work week, with rain chances in the 15 to 
  30% range.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
(Tonight through next Monday)
Issued at 1156 PM CDT Mon Aug 3 2026

A typical summertime pattern continues as we sit between two 
systems with an upper-level ridge to our west and an upper-level 
low to our east. At the surface, high pressure in the eastern Gulf
will keep our winds from the south but with no surface low to 
increase our pressure gradient, winds will remain light. Because 
we are between two upper-level lows, our winds aloft are from the 
north, pushing dry continental air into our upper and mid levels. 
This dry air is present in our 0Z sounding with a strong cap at 
700 mb. While we have been getting some convection, it has been 
limited to the sea breeze and has been shallow. The mixing of the 
dry air aloft to the surface has helped keep our dew points in the
low to mid 70s and has kept the afternoon heat index around 105, 
which is below the 108 needed for an advisory. Soundings over the 
previous 24 hours do show an increase in moisture aloft, which is 
in line with model expectations.


For the second half of the week, the upper-level lows will
dissipate and ridging will begin to build over the region. Global
models keep the main ridge axis to our north. Rain chances will
remain between 40% and 60% with showers mainly being diurnally
driven.

&&

.AVIATION...
(06Z TAFS)
Issued at 1156 PM CDT Mon Aug 3 2026

Conditions will be VFR with MVFR impacts near sunrise. During the
daytime on Tuesday conditions will be VFR with light south winds.

&&

.MARINE...
Issued at 1156 PM CDT Mon Aug 3 2026

Light south to southwest flow will continue for the rest of the
week. Waves will stay below 3 feet. Rain chances will remain low
for the next several days, around 10%.

&&

.FIRE WEATHER...
Issued at 1156 PM CDT Mon Aug 3 2026

KBDI values continue to climb, sitting between 500 to 600 across
the region. Minimum RH values will start to increase from 40% to
60% from Tuesday to Friday. Rain chances will increase during the
second half of the week with isolated showers during the
afternoon.
